Alaska's FY2024 ratios therefore blend ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of the combined carrier, and are not directly comparable to a full-year combined entity or to the other four carriers' organic years.
- The other four carriers are all calendar-year FY2024 filers with comparable income-statement line items ("aircraft fuel" and "salaries, wages and benefits") [airlines_costs_fy2024.txt]. Note that line-item definitions still vary modestly by carrier (e.g., what is loaded into the fuel line vs. taxes/refinery activity, and whether regional-carrier labor sits in the salaries line or in a purchased-capacity line), so gaps of a few tenths of a point are within definitional noise.

**Salaries, wages and benefits as % of revenue:** Delta 26.22% → United 29.23% → American 29.55% → Alaska 30.58% → Southwest 44.54%. Southwest's outlier labor ratio is consistent with its very thin FY2024 operating income of $321M on $27,483M of revenue [airlines_costs_fy2024.txt].
